title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple silicon
gist: The most-used local runner swapped its Apple-silicon backend to MLX, added a 4-bit weight format from NVIDIA, and reworked its prompt cache to be reused across conversations and to keep shared prefixes. A June follow-up fuses operations into single Metal kernels and moves sampling to the GPU.
changes: Local stacks are getting the same class of work as datacenter engines (kernel fusion, cache retention policy), about a year behind and done by hand.
caveats: The comparison changes engine and quantisation at once and does not name the chip. Needs more than 32 GB of memory. A competitor found its draft model barely drafting on some models.

bears_on.note: Serious optimisation is reaching local runtimes. People are doing it, by hand, for everyone at once.

retired_why: Out of scope. On 19 Nov the reader clarified that local means fitted to what you have (different devices), not on-device hardware, so the on-device question is no longer tracked.
